title: WHAT THIS APP CHANGES (AND WHAT IT DOES NOT)

qa.q: Can this get me banned by Valve Anti-Cheat (VAC)?
qa.a: Only Valve decides what VAC acts on, so this app makes no promise about it. What the app does (checked in its source code): it edits CS2 config files (autoexec.cfg), changes standard Windows settings (power plan, Game DVR, fullscreen optimizations, DNS), reads game state through Valve's Game State Integration, can raise CS2's process priority, and can type a 'connect' command into the CS2 console for you. It does not read or modify CS2 memory, inject DLLs or patch game files. Hobby project, not affiliated with Valve. Use at your own risk.

qa.q: Can I undo all changes made by the application?
qa.a: Yes! Clicking the [⏪ Restore Defaults] button on the top right instantly restores Windows Game DVR, restores your default Windows power plan, reenables fullscreen optimizations, and resets the autoexec configuration back to clean stock defaults.

qa.q: Does this app communicate with external servers or collect telemetry?
qa.a: There are no ads, no accounts and no tracking, and the app never sends your Steam login, files or personal data anywhere. It does contact these places: game servers directly (UDP A2S queries for player counts, maps and ping); ZE Graph (zegraph.xyz) for the GFL round scores, country mix and map pictures; geronimohq.com for the signed update check and the same server totals the website shows; and the Discord app on your own PC through a local pipe. Steam, the Steam workshop and your browser only open when you click something.

qa.q: How do updates work?
qa.a: The app checks geronimohq.com for a signed update manifest. The new exe is only offered when its Ed25519 signature, size and SHA-256 match, so a tampered file is rejected. Settings shows the last check and a Check now button. Your settings and logs are kept when the app updates.

qa.q: Does it find Steam and CS2 if they are on another drive or in another library?
qa.a: Yes. The app asks Steam itself: its registry entries, its list of game libraries, and the file that says where Counter-Strike 2 is installed (even under a custom folder name). It also checks the usual folders on your fixed drives. Network and removable drives are never probed. If CS2 or Steam is moved while the app is open, restart the app.

qa.q: The app window does not open and a message mentions WebView2. What is that?
qa.a: The app window is drawn by the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, a free Microsoft component that Windows 11 and up-to-date Windows 10 already have. If it is missing, the app shows a message with a button that opens Microsoft's download page. Install the 'Evergreen Bootstrapper' and start the app again.

qa.q: What does disabling Windows Game DVR do?
qa.a: Windows Game DVR continuously runs background video capture hooks inside the Windows Desktop Window Manager (DWM). Disabling it frees up GPU/CPU encoding pipelines, directly eliminating micro-stutters and sudden FPS drops during heavy combat and smoke grenades.

qa.q: What does 'Disable Fullscreen Optimizations' (Direct-Flip) do?
qa.a: Windows 10/11 forces games into a hybrid borderless presentation mode that routes frames through the Windows compositor. Disabling fullscreen optimizations on cs2.exe grants the game exclusive hardware display access (Direct-Flip mode), eliminating DWM compositor latency and reducing click-to-photon mouse input lag.

qa.q: Why does the app select AMD Balanced for Ryzen 3D V-Cache (X3D) processors?
qa.a: If you have an AMD Ryzen 5700X3D, 5800X3D, 7800X3D, or 9800X3D, setting power to generic Ultimate Performance can interfere with AMD's Collaborative Processor Performance Control (CPPC). AMD Balanced allows CPPC to correctly schedule CS2 threads onto the ultra-fast 3D V-Cache cores, giving you maximum 1% low FPS.

qa.q: What happens on standard non-X3D CPUs and Intel hybrid processors?
qa.a: For standard AMD processors (e.g., Ryzen 5600X, 7600), the app applies High Performance to ensure clocks never downthrottle. For Intel 12th/13th/14th Gen hybrid CPUs with P-cores and E-cores, High Performance combined with High Process Priority ensures the Windows kernel schedules CS2's render loop exclusively on physical Performance cores.

qa.q: Why should I purge DirectX & Vulkan shader caches?
qa.a: After GPU driver updates (NVIDIA/AMD) or CS2 game patches, old compiled shader caches can become corrupted or misaligned, leading to severe stutter when rendering smokes, fire, and particle effects. Purging the cache allows the driver to recompile fresh, optimized shaders on clean launch.

qa.q: What does 'Clean CS2 crash dumps & temp files' delete?
qa.a: Only crash reports: .dmp files and crash_*.txt in the CS2 bin and csgo folders, the contents of csgo\dumps, and CS2 minidumps in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps. It never deletes console.log or other .log files, because the Log Analyzer and the Discord server detection read console.log.

qa.q: The app said 'Finished with problems'. What does that mean?
qa.a: One or more steps of Optimize, Restore, Clean-up or a repair tool could not do their job, for example a power plan that does not exist on your PC, a Windows tool that returned an error, or a step that needs Administrator. Every other step still ran. The activity log marks each failed step with [ERROR] and says why. The app no longer shows a plain success message when a step failed.

qa.q: My PC has no 'High Performance' power plan. What happens?
qa.a: Many laptops hide that plan. The app asks Windows to create it again from its built-in definition. If Windows refuses, the log says so with [ERROR] and your current plan is kept. Nothing is switched to a different plan behind your back.

title: NETWORK OPTIMIZATION, GAMING DNS PROS & CONS & PACKET LOSS

qa.q: What does the DNS Optimizer change, and how do I undo it?
qa.a:
DNS (Domain Name System) translates domain names into IP addresses. Besides speeding up domain lookups for Steam SDR relays, Workshop FastDL map servers, Discord voice channels, and web browsing, custom DNS resolvers serve multiple purposes:
• Reliability: Bypasses congested or malfunctioning default ISP DNS servers.
• Security (Quad9 9.9.9.9): Automatically blocks known malware, phishing, and spyware domains before they can load.
• Ad & Telemetry Filtering (AdGuard 94.140.14.14): Blocks background ad-trackers and Windows/app telemetry domains that cause random bandwidth spikes.
• Privacy (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1): Prevents your ISP from logging or hijacking your DNS queries.
• How it works: the standard Windows 'netsh' command changes the DNS of your active network adapter (a Windows setting, needs Administrator). No drivers are installed. A 1-click 'Restore ISP Default (DHCP)' button undoes it.

qa.q: What are the honest Pros and Cons (Limitations) of changing DNS?
qa.a:
✅ PROS:
• Faster initial connections to Steam relays, FastDL custom map mirrors, Discord, and websites.
• Lower lookup jitter and protection against ISP DNS outages.
• Optional built-in malware protection (Quad9) or telemetry/ad blocking (AdGuard).

⚠️ CONS / LIMITATIONS:
• Does NOT reduce raw in-game UDP ping once already connected to a server IP (because active game traffic sends UDP packets directly to the server IP without querying DNS).
• Choosing a physically distant DNS server without benchmarking first can cause CDNs (like Steam downloads) to route you to a farther download mirror — always click '⚡ Benchmark All DNS Servers' first!
• Hotel, school, or airport Wi-Fi login portals sometimes require default DHCP DNS to display their sign-in page (if needed, click '↺ Restore ISP Default (DHCP)').

qa.q: Can standalone PC software eliminate ISP packet loss without multi-path VPN routing tunnels?
qa.a: While standalone local software cannot physically reroute undersea ISP fiber cables, CS2 Command Center applies all safe, official Windows and CS2 network optimizations: 1) Benchmarks and configures low-jitter DNS resolvers and flushes stale DNS cache; 2) Disables Windows Network Throttling Index (MMCSS) so Windows never throttles non-multimedia game UDP packets; 3) Configures optimal sub-tick packet rates in autoexec (rate 1000000); 4) Guides you on using CS2's built-in packet buffering to smooth out ISP jitter.

qa.q: What does CS2's 'Buffering to smooth over packet loss' (cl_net_buffer_ticks) do?
qa.a: Under Settings -> Game -> Telemetry: Setting 'Buffering to smooth packet loss' to 'None' (cl_net_buffer_ticks 0) provides the absolute lowest latency on flawless fiber connections. If your ISP suffers from packet loss or jitter, set it to '1 Packet' (cl_net_buffer_ticks 1) or '2 Packets' (cl_net_buffer_ticks 2). This creates a 15-30ms jitter buffer that reassembles missing packets before rendering, completely preventing rubberbanding and micro-teleports during heavy gunfights.

qa.q: Why do Zombie Escape & 64-player servers experience choke or stutter?
qa.a: In 64-player community servers, the server broadcasts massive amounts of entity updates, particle data, and zombie positions every tick. Setting 'rate 1000000' (maximum 8 Mbps bandwidth allocation) prevents your client from dropping entity packets when 60 players shoot and throw grenades simultaneously.

qa.q: Which network adapter does the DNS change use, and does it work on non-English Windows?
qa.a: The one Windows really uses to reach the internet (its default route), asked from Windows directly, so it works in any Windows language, on Wi-Fi or cable, and ignores virtual adapters such as VPN or Hyper-V. Restore changes the same adapter back to automatic DNS.

qa.q: What competitive settings are installed into autoexec.cfg?
qa.a: It writes one marked block to autoexec.cfg: fps_max 0, engine_low_latency_sleep_after_client_tick, snd_mixahead 0.025, rate 1000000 (bytes per second; CS2 may cap it), cl_net_buffer_ticks 0, animated avatars off, and the frame-time / ping / packet-loss HUD graphs. It does not add jumpthrow, C4-drop or other gameplay binds.

qa.q: Why is snd_mixahead set to 0.025 instead of the default 0.05?
qa.a: The default Source 2 audio buffer (0.05) creates 50ms of audio latency between gunshots/footsteps and your speakers. Setting snd_mixahead to 0.025 cuts audio processing latency in half (25ms), allowing you to hear enemy footsteps, zombie screams, and grenade bounces a full frame earlier.

qa.q: Will applying autoexec overwrite my custom bindings or crosshair?
qa.a: No! If an existing autoexec.cfg is present, the app backs it up and non-destructively appends or updates only the competitive performance blocks, keeping your personal binds, crosshair, sensitivity, and custom aliases in place (only the app's own marked block is added or replaced).

qa.q: Which launch options are recommended and why?
qa.a: Recommended flags: -novid (skips intro video for faster game startup), -high (launches with High CPU priority), -threads <N> (matches engine worker threads to physical CPU cores), -nojoy (disables joystick polling overhead to save CPU cycles), and +fps_max 0 (uncaps framerate for minimum input delay).

qa.q: Why shouldn't obsolete CS:GO launch options (-tickrate 128, -d3d9ex, +mat_queue_mode) be used in CS2?
qa.a: Counter-Strike 2 runs on Valve's modern Source 2 engine with a sub-tick network model and DirectX 11 / Vulkan graphics. Legacy Source 1 options like -tickrate 128, -d3d9ex, and +mat_queue_mode no longer exist in the engine; using them can generate engine console warnings and cause unstable thread scheduling.

qa.q: What does the Live Booster & Gaming DNS Optimizer do?
qa.a: The Live Booster safely elevates cs2.exe CPU thread priority to High (Win32 HIGH_PRIORITY_CLASS) without using risky 'RAM Cleaners' that cause browser/Discord crashes and page-fault stutters. The Gaming DNS Optimizer benchmarks 6 global gaming DNS providers (Cloudflare, Google, Quad9, OpenDNS, Level3, AdGuard) in parallel for real latency and jitter, letting you apply the fastest DNS or restore ISP defaults in 1 click.

qa.q: Are the Optimizer and PC Maintenance meant to increase my max FPS?
qa.a: They are NOT meant to artificially inflate maximum FPS beyond your physical CPU/GPU limits. Instead, they are engineered for System Stability, Frame-Time Consistency (1% Lows), Micro-Stutter Prevention during 64-player Zombie Escape & heavy utility, Display/Alt-Tab Reliability (MPO), Sub-Tick & DNS Network Responsiveness, and SSD/OS Health.

qa.q: Does 'Apply to Steam' change the launch options of my other games?
qa.a: No. The app edits only Counter-Strike 2's own entry in the Steam account that logged in last, and leaves every other game and every other line of the file as it was. Quotes and backslashes in your options are saved correctly. If the file cannot be read safely, nothing is written. Steam must be closed first: if Steam is running the app refuses to save, because Steam would overwrite the change when it exits. A backup (localconfig.vdf.backup) is kept next to the file.

qa.q: How does the Slot Sniper function and how does it detect open slots?
qa.a: The Slot Sniper runs a high-speed 0.25s background polling loop that queries the server directly via standard Steam A2S_INFO UDP protocol. It checks live player counts against your selected slot threshold (Normal public players: up to 61, Mapper or Supporter: up to 62, VIP or Admin: up to 63). The instant a player leaves or disconnects, the sniper detects the open slot within milliseconds, executes the in-game console connect immediately, and starts a 10-second cooldown. It only starts while CS2 is running.

qa.q: Why doesn't the Slot Sniper continuously spam 'connect' in the CS2 console while waiting?
qa.a: While it is technically possible to spam 'connect' in the CS2 console every second, doing so causes Counter-Strike 2's networking subsystem (Steam Datagram Relay) and Source 2's unmanaged heap allocator to hold undrained connection sessions and console string buffers. This causes CS2's RAM usage to stack up, climbing higher and higher (4GB -> 6GB -> 8GB+), which is neither safe nor appropriate for PC stability. Instead, the Slot Sniper uses True Silent Sniping: it watches the server silently via external UDP A2S queries at 0.25s (taking 0 CS2 RAM and 0 clipboard usage), and the exact millisecond a player disconnects, it executes the in-game console connect immediately with a 10-second cooldown.

qa.q: What happens if someone connects faster than me?
qa.a: On popular 64/64 servers like GFL, multiple players may be attempting to join simultaneously. If another player connects a split-second faster, CS2 displays the standard server full notification. The Command Center recognizes that you have not entered the server yet; you can re-arm the sniper with a single click or leave it armed to immediately catch the very next open slot!

qa.q: How does the Command Center know when I am already in the server?
qa.a: The app combines automatic signals: the connection line CS2 writes to console.log (needs -condebug in your launch options, which you can type in the Launch Options tab), Valve Game State Integration (GSI) via local HTTP events, the map name matched against the server list, and your Steam name found in a live A2S player roster. When you connect, the app switches to tracking mode and disarms the sniper so it never fires duplicate connections.

qa.q: What are the Slot Sniper Priority Tiers (VIP / Mapper / Normal)?
qa.a: On 64-player community servers like GFL ZE the last slots are reserved for VIPs, Mappers and Supporters. Use GFL slot priority on the GFL card: Normal (up to 61) for public players, Mapper / Supporter (up to 62), or VIP / Admin (up to 63). This avoids the 'Server is reserved' kick. The three buttons next to the server filter set the same target for every other server.

qa.q: What does 'Map not installed. Get it' mean?
qa.a: The server is playing a Zombie Escape map that is not on your PC, so joining would fail with 'Required map is missing on your client'. The amber link appears on the server's row, or next to Copy IP on the GFL card. Click it and Steam opens that map's workshop page. Press Subscribe, Steam downloads it in the background, and the warning disappears within about 20 seconds of the map appearing in your folders. If the app does not know a map's workshop page, the click opens a workshop search for the map name instead. Downloading the map through another tool does not work: CS2 only uses workshop maps that Steam itself downloaded.

qa.q: What is the 'Launch Delay' setting for?
qa.a: When CS2 is closed and you click 'Connect to GFL', the Command Center launches the game via Steam and waits for the configured Launch Delay (default: 15 seconds) so CS2 can load its main menu and establish Steam network credentials before executing the direct server connection.

qa.q: What does '4:46 on map' and the '≥' sign mean?
qa.a: It is how long the current map has been running. The app reads the longest player connection time on the server, because a player's time restarts on a map change; GFL uses ZE Graph's exact start time. A time with '≥' in front is a minimum: the app only knows the map has run at least that long, for example on an empty server or right after the app opened. It becomes exact once the app sees a map change or has a player to measure.

qa.q: What is the Geo radar and how accurate is it?
qa.a: It is an estimate of where the players on a server come from, shown as Country or Region (your choice per server). It uses name signals and the time of day the players are active, so it is never exact and no individual player is identified. The coloured pills fill the card's width, up to two lines, and the rest are grouped under '+N more' (hover for the list).

qa.q: What does 'N bots excluded' or 'MOSTLY BOTS' mean?
qa.a: Some servers fill empty slots with bots. The app counts humans only: bots are subtracted from the player count. 'N bots excluded' shows how many were removed. 'MOSTLY BOTS' appears when bots are at least half of the reported players (and at least three), because the headline number would otherwise look busier than the server really is.

qa.q: How does Planet China work, and why is there no Players button there?
qa.a: Planet China lists the Chinese communities in clusters (EXG, FyS, MoeUB, ZL, 93X). Pick a cluster in 'Select community cluster' and only its servers are listed and queried. Chinese servers block the live player list (A2S_PLAYER), so the Players dialog and name-based features are not offered there. Player counts, ping and map still work.

qa.q: If I play a different game, will it still show up? Does this custom presence only affect CS2?
qa.a: This custom presence ONLY affects Counter-Strike 2! It will never interfere with other games. When CS2 is closed, the Command Center completely closes the Discord RPC session. When you play other games (Apex, Dota 2, Rust, etc.), Discord's native game detection or that game's own rich presence will show completely normally.

qa.q: Why does Discord show nothing when CS2 is closed?
qa.a: By design. When CS2 is closed, nothing is sent, so Discord shows no game from this app.

qa.q: How does the app know which server I am on?
qa.a: In this order: the connection line CS2 writes to console.log (needs -condebug in your launch options, which you can type in the Launch Options tab), the map the game reports matched against the servers, and your Steam name found in a server's player roster. If none of these identify the server yet, Discord shows the generic card 'Zombie Escape Server' with the map and a GeronimoHQ Portal button, then switches to the full card as soon as the server is known. The activity log lists every card sent.

qa.q: Do new users need to create or configure a Discord Application ID?
qa.a: No. The app ships with its own Discord Application ID. Rich Presence works completely out-of-the-box for all users with zero extra setup or developer portal steps.

qa.q: Why don't the buttons [🎮 Server IP] and [💬 Community Discord] show when I view my own profile?
qa.a: Discord's client intentionally hides Rich Presence action buttons on your OWN profile popout (Discord does this to prevent users from clicking links on their own profile). Rest assured, your friends, teammates, and server members CAN see and click both buttons directly on your profile!

qa.q: How do I turn the presence off?
qa.a: Use the 'Enable Discord Rich Presence' switch on the Discord Presence tab. Off clears your card and stops sending until you switch it back on. 'Refresh now' only forces an immediate update. While CS2 is closed nothing is sent anyway.

title: CUSTOM ZE MAP CLEANER & STORAGE HYGIENE

qa.q: Why should I clean custom maps?
qa.a: Custom Zombie Escape maps downloaded from the Steam workshop are stored as .vpk packages (mostly in steamapps/workshop/content/730) and can range from 50 MB to 2.5 GB each. Over time, active ZE players accumulate tens or hundreds of GB of stale map packages. The cleaner lets you sort by file size or last played date and delete the maps you no longer need. Subscribed server map packs, server asset packs and official Valve maps are protected and cannot be ticked.

qa.q: What happens if I delete a map and later rejoin a server running that map?
qa.a: When you join a server that plays it again, CS2 asks 'Confirm Workshop Download' and downloads the map from the Steam workshop after you accept. Deleting downloaded maps only removes files that can be downloaded again; it does not affect your account. The app asks you to confirm before it deletes anything, and the confirmation cannot be undone.

qa.q: How does the Map Cleaner make sure protected maps are not deleted?
qa.a: When you press Delete, the app scans again with the protection choices shown on screen at that moment and deletes only what is still unprotected and still on disk. Subscribed server packs and server asset packs can never be ticked, and anything that became protected since you ticked it is skipped and reported.

qa.q: What do SSD TRIM, SFC, and DISM do?
qa.a: SSD TRIM instructs your solid-state drive controller to reclaim unused memory blocks, maintaining peak NAND write speeds and low read latency. SFC (System File Checker) scans and repairs corrupted Windows core system files. DISM repairs the Windows Component Store image using official Microsoft files.

qa.q: Does clearing Discord & Steam web cache log me out of my accounts?
qa.a: No! The cleaner specifically targets cached images, stickers, and Chromium/CEF web data in the Cache folders. It never touches login tokens, saved passwords, or session cookies.

qa.q: What do 'Verify Workshop VPK health' and 'Repair corrupted VPKs' check, and what can they miss?
qa.a: Verify reads every workshop pack under steamapps/workshop/content/730 (all your Steam libraries that hold CS2) and checks the pack's index and that every data part it points to is on disk and long enough. That finds downloads that stopped half way, missing or short archive parts, empty or unreadable files, wrong file signatures and folders with leftover temporary files. It cannot see changed bytes inside a file that is complete and the right size, because that would mean reading every file in full. Repair removes only the packs Verify flagged. It refuses anything that is not a plain workshop item folder, never follows links, and skips a pack that changed in the last 15 minutes because Steam may still be downloading it. Removed packs are not sent to the recycle bin. A subscribed map is downloaded again by Steam on its next check, or when you join a server that needs it; maps you only played once are asked for again with a download dialog.

qa.q: Which temporary files does the Windows temp clean-up delete?
qa.a: Files in your %TEMP% folder and in Windows\Temp that are older than 24 hours and not in use. Anything newer is left alone because a running program or an installer may still need it, and the app never touches its own unpacked files or the temporary folders of other single-file apps. Locked files are skipped.

qa.q: Windows asks for another administrator's password when I use Relaunch as Administrator. Is that a problem?
qa.a: No, but it matters for two things. The elevated copy still uses your own settings, logs and Steam folders. Windows settings that are stored per user (Game DVR, Start with Windows) are saved for the account that approved the prompt, and the activity log says so. Changes that apply to the whole PC (power plan, DNS, MPO commands) work the same either way.

qa.q: SFC, DISM and TRIM take a long time. Do they block the rest of the app?
qa.a: No. They run in their own slot, so Optimize, Restore, the Map Cleaner and updates still work. Only one of these long tools runs at a time. The app stops waiting after 30 minutes (TRIM), 60 minutes (SFC) or 90 minutes (DISM) and tells you. The result is reported from Windows' own exit codes and also works on non-English Windows.

qa.q: Why does the Log Analyzer show 'N/A' instead of a grade?
qa.a: A grade needs a readable console.log. If there is none yet (add -condebug to your launch options and play a session) or it cannot be read, the analyzer says so instead of showing a good grade. More than 15 frame or network events grade B, more than 40 grade C.

title: GPU MPO DIAGNOSTICS & TROUBLESHOOTER (AMD, NVIDIA & INTEL)

qa.q: Why is GPU MPO Diagnostics included in CS2 Command Center?
qa.a: Multi-Plane Overlay (MPO) is one of the most common root causes of Alt-Tab black screens, display freezes, Discord/Chrome checkerboard glitches, and GPU driver crashes (such as AMD Driver Timeout or NVIDIA TDR) while playing CS2. CS2 Command Center provides this dedicated diagnostic tab so players can understand their MPO configuration, test for display issues, and access official AMD/NVIDIA resolution steps.

qa.q: Is the GPU MPO Diagnostics tab safe? Does it modify my registry automatically?
qa.a: The GPU MPO Diagnostics tab is read-only: it makes no registry edits and does not alter your display driver automatically. It provides live hardware and registry inspection, clear technical explanations, and safe 1-click clipboard helpers for manual user review.

qa.q: Should I disable Windows Multi-Plane Overlay (MPO)?
qa.a: If your system runs smoothly with zero black screen flickers, driver timeouts, or dual-monitor stutter, keep MPO enabled (Windows default). If you suffer from 1-3 second Alt-Tab black screens, AMD driver timeouts, Discord checkerboard glitches, or G-Sync stutter with mixed refresh rates, disabling MPO via the registry is an officially verified, safe workaround.

qa.q: What should I do before disabling MPO? Should I use DDU or AMD Cleanup Utility?
qa.a:
Before touching MPO registry settings, you should ALWAYS first perform a clean display driver wipe and reinstall using Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) by Wagnardsoft in Windows Safe Mode, and check if that solved your problem. Many black screens and timeouts are fixed by a fresh driver install alone!

⚠️ Why avoid AMD Cleanup Utility: Manufacturer cleanup tools like AMD Cleanup Utility often remove critical Windows chipset drivers, USB root hubs, and PCIe bus drivers, which can cause broken mouse/keyboard input or Safe Mode boot loops. DDU is isolated specifically to graphics display drivers.

qa.q: How do the Minimize [-] and Close [X] buttons work?
qa.a: [X] always closes the app completely. [-] depends on the setting 'Minimize to the system tray when [-] is clicked' (on by default): on, the window hides in the tray near the clock; off, it minimizes to the taskbar like any window. Clicking the app's taskbar button also minimizes it.

qa.q: How do I restore the app from the system tray?
qa.a: Simply left-click or right-click the orange CS2 icon in your Windows system tray near the clock, or launch the app shortcut again. You can also right-click the tray icon to quick-connect to GFL, toggle the Slot Sniper, or click [❌ Exit Completely].

qa.q: How much memory and CPU does the app use?
qa.a: The window is drawn by Microsoft Edge WebView2, which Task Manager lists separately from CS2_Command_Center. In our tests the whole app used roughly 500 to 600 MB while open (most of it WebView2), the animated backdrop uses a small share of one CPU core, and the memory drops sharply while the window is minimized or in the tray (about 190 MB in our test) because the app asks WebView2 for its low-memory mode and hands unused memory back to Windows. It grows again when you use the window. The two CS2_Command_Center lines in Task Manager are normal: a tiny launcher and the app itself.
